title: After 60, a walk was never just a walk.
deck: Risk of heart disease after 60, vs the 25% who walk least

annotations.detail: A fifth of the risk gone
Half the risk at the top

_provenance.paper: doi:10.1161_circulationaha.122.061288 · Paluch et al. 2022, Circulation · harmonized meta-analysis of 8 prospective device-measured cohorts, n=20,152, mean follow-up 6.2y, 1,523 CVD events
_provenance.axis: The paper reports study-specific quartiles of device-measured daily steps; step counts per quartile are not in the abstract, so x = population percentile with points at quarter midpoints (12.5/37.5/62.5/87.5). The counter counts rank, not steps — nothing on screen implies step volumes.
_provenance.stratum: Curve is the OLDER-adult stratum (≥60) only, per the deck ('after 60'). n=20,152 on the source line is the whole meta-analysis; the abstract does not report the older stratum's n. The younger-adult arm (c4–c6: HR 0.79/0.90/0.95, all CIs crossing 1.0) is caption material, explicitly attributed.
_provenance.reference: Lowest quartile of daily steps among adults ≥60 — HR 1.00 by definition; the (12.5, 100, 'baseline') point is the comparator, not a reported estimate

claims.quote: For older adults, the HR for quartile 2 was 0.80 (95% CI, 0.69 to 0.93)
and 0.51 for quartile 4 (95% CI, 0.41 to 0.63) compared with the lowest quartile.

_provenance.copy_grounding: 'A fifth of the risk gone' ← c1 (HR 0.80 = −20%). 'Half the risk at the top' ← c3 (HR 0.51 = −49%). Outcome named 'heart disease' in the deck ← CVD events defined as 'fatal and nonfatal coronary heart disease, stroke, and heart failure'.
_provenance.reveal_test: Headline names the walking-after-60 belief ('just a walk') and withholds what a walk actually buys; the curve supplies it and −49% is the completion payoff. 'THE FIRST STEP UP' flag is on screen from t≈0.2s while the baseline segment holds.
_provenance.honesty: Deltas shrink as steps rise (−20 → −18 → −11 percentage points of HR), so no copy claims the fall accelerates; 'THE PAYOFF / Half the risk at the top' states the endpoint, not a rate. Younger-arm null goes to the caption — never a second lane on this chart.
